column4: Mechanism on the Pi 5 gateway
Per-source token-bucket / connection-rate limit on the gateway firewall for the offending 5-tuple or source.
SYN cookies, half-open connection caps, conntrack table limits, ICMP/UDP rate caps.
Drop/blackhole the attacking source address with an escalating TTL (5 -> 15 -> 60 min).
Close the abused destination port or protocol at the gateway for that device.
Drop unsolicited SYN/FIN/NULL/Xmas probes and ICMP sweeps; suppress port-unreachable replies.
Deny outbound to the observed command-and-control endpoint; DNS sinkhole the domain on the local resolver.
Block the offending prefix / subnet when many sources share it, instead of thousands of single rules.
Fair-queue and cap the victim device's share of uplink so the flood cannot starve neighbouring devices.
Move the device to an isolated VLAN that reaches only the gateway (management and telemetry only).
Drop frames from the offending MAC at the bridge; deauthenticate / disassociate the wireless client.
Deny all traffic to and from the device except the controller heartbeat channel.
Install static ARP bindings for gateway and device; broadcast corrective gratuitous ARP; flush poisoned caches.
Enable dynamic ARP inspection and DHCP snooping; drop offers from any non-authorised server.
Reject plaintext HTTP / MQTT / DNS for that device; pin traffic to TLS and to the gateway's DoT resolver.
Rotate PSK, re-issue device certificate, invalidate key material that may have been observed.
Ban the source after N failed authentications with exponential back-off (jail-style rule set).
Lock or throttle the specific account being guessed rather than the whole service.
Force a new admin password / API token / MQTT credential for the device and its gateway record.
Disable Telnet and password login, enforce key or certificate auth, restrict management ports to a gateway allowlist.
Kill active sessions, invalidate cookies and bearer tokens, force re-authentication.
Restart the affected daemon on the device or its gateway-side proxy to clear exhausted resources.
Terminate the malicious process and remove its persistence (init entry, cron job, watchdog respawn).
Insert a reverse-proxy rule at the gateway blocking the observed payload class (injection, traversal, upload abuse).
Turn off the vulnerable endpoint, remote web UI, UPnP, or other non-essential service.
Tighten body size, header and timeout limits; enforce strict input validation at the proxy.
Bounce the device's interface and re-DHCP without a full reboot.
Reboot via device API or SSH; clears memory-resident state.
Toggle the smart plug, PoE port or GPIO relay feeding the device when it is unresponsive.
Push the last known-good configuration snapshot held by the gateway.
Reset to factory defaults, then re-provision inside quarantine with fresh unique credentials.
Re-flash a signed known-good image, or roll back to the previous verified version.
Start full packet capture and verbose host logging for the incident window (evidence; always parallel).
Redirect the attacker's flows to a deception service to profile behaviour without exposing the real device.
Lower the detection threshold and shorten the inference window for this device temporarily.
Fold confirmed-benign behaviour back into the device profile / incremental model.
Dashboard alert plus out-of-band message with the incident timeline and the actions already tried.
Keep the device isolated pending manual review; block automatic release.
Generate machine- and human-readable reports, including the peer-device sweep results.
